title: Diogenes the Wise Man
author: James Baldwin
summary: 第欧根尼住在木桶里，只求亚历山大大帝别挡住他的阳光。
publicDomainBasis: Published 1896 by the American Book Company; author James Baldwin (1841–1925). Public domain in the United States and in China (author's life plus 70 years).

paragraphs.en: At Corinth, in Greece, there lived a very wise man whose name was Diogenes. Men came from all parts of the land to see him and hear him talk.
paragraphs.zh: 在希腊的科林斯，住着一位非常有智慧的人，名叫第欧根尼。各地的人都来见他、听他谈话。

paragraphs.en: But wise as he was, he had some very queer ways. He did not believe that any man ought to have more things than he really needed; and he said that no man needed much. And so he did not live in a house, but slept in a tub or barrel, which he rolled about from place to place. He spent his days sitting in the sun, and saying wise things to those who were around him.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管他很智慧，却有些非常古怪的习惯。他认为人不该拥有超过真正需要的东西，还说人其实需要得很少。因此他不住房子，而是睡在一只木桶里，把木桶滚来滚去，四处为家。他白天坐在阳光下，对围在身边的人说些充满智慧的话。

paragraphs.en: At noon one day, Diogenes was seen walking through the streets with a lighted lantern, and looking all around as if in search of something.
paragraphs.zh: 一天中午，有人看见第欧根尼提着一盏点亮的灯笼走在街上，四处张望，仿佛在寻找什么。

paragraphs.en: "Why do you carry a lantern when the sun is shining?" some one said.
paragraphs.zh: “太阳这么大，你为什么还提着灯笼？”有人问。

paragraphs.en: "I am looking for an honest man," answered Diogenes.
paragraphs.zh: “我在找一个诚实的人。”第欧根尼回答。

paragraphs.en: When Alexander the Great went to Corinth, all the foremost men in the city came out to see him and to praise him. But Diogenes did not come; and he was the only man for whose opinions Alexander cared.
paragraphs.zh: 亚历山大大帝来到科林斯时，城里所有显要人物都出来迎接他、赞美他。可第欧根尼没有来；而亚历山大事事在意的，恰恰是这个人的看法。

paragraphs.en: And so, since the wise man would not come to see the king, the king went to see the wise man. He found Diogenes in an out-of-the-way place, lying on the ground by his tub. He was enjoying the heat and the light of the sun.
paragraphs.zh: 既然这位智者不肯来见国王，国王便亲自去见他。国王在一个偏僻的地方找到了第欧根尼，他正躺在木桶旁的地上，享受着阳光的温暖和明亮。

paragraphs.en: When he saw the king and a great many people coming, he sat up and looked at Alexander. Alexander greeted him and said,—
paragraphs.zh: 看见国王带着一大群人走来，他坐起身，看着亚历山大。亚历山大向他问好，说：

paragraphs.en: "Diogenes, I have heard a great deal about your wisdom. Is there anything that I can do for you?"
paragraphs.zh: “第欧根尼，我听过许多关于你智慧的事。有什么我能为你做的吗？”

paragraphs.en: "Yes," said Diogenes. "You can stand a little on one side, so as not to keep the sunshine from me."
paragraphs.zh: “有，”第欧根尼说，“你往旁边站一点，别挡住我的阳光。”

paragraphs.en: This answer was so different from what he expected, that the king was much surprised. But it did not make him angry; it only made him admire the strange man all the more. When he turned to ride back, he said to his officers,—
paragraphs.zh: 这个回答完全出乎国王意料，他十分惊讶。但国王并没有生气，反而更加钦佩这个怪人。他转身上马回去时，对身边的军官说：

paragraphs.en: "Say what you will; if I were not Alexander, I would like to be Diogenes."
paragraphs.zh: “随你们怎么说；如果我不是亚历山大，我倒愿意做第欧根尼。”
